articles.title: APPLE APPARENTLY TESTED A STYLUS FOR THE FOLDABLE IPHONE, THEN NIXED THE IDEA
articles.summary: Apple reportedly explored and even prototyped a smaller Apple Pencil designed for the upcoming foldable iPhone Ultra, with plans for magnetic attachment and charging similar to the iPad. However, the company apparently abandoned the idea because a stylus could interfere with the folding mechanism and potentially damage the softer surface of the foldable display. While an Apple Pencil is unlikely to launch alongside the first-generation foldable iPhone, the concept may return in future models if foldable screen technology becomes more durable.

articles.title: GEMINI OMNI 1.1 FLASH LETS YOU BUILD WITH MORE CONTROL
articles.summary: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash gives developers more control over AI-generated video, moving the model closer to a production-ready creative tool rather than a simple video generator. The update can extend existing scenes while maintaining visual and narrative consistency, generate smooth transitions between specified first and last frames, and use video references to preserve characters and motion. It also adds faster, lower-cost 360p drafts for experimentation and upscaling to 1080p or 4K for finished work.

articles.title: APPLE WILL BE LAUNCHING ITS FIRST PAIR OF SMART GLASSES NEXT YEAR: HERE'S WHAT'S COMING
articles.summary: Apple is reportedly preparing AI-powered smart glasses for launch in 2027 that focus on voice and camera-based assistance rather than augmented reality displays. The glasses would use Siri and Visual Intelligence to analyze the user's surroundings, answer questions, provide context, translate signs, and save visual reminders, while also functioning as open-ear audio devices. Apple is developing multiple frame styles and premium finishes in-house, with future versions potentially adding health features such as heart-rate monitoring. Unlike Meta's smart glasses, Apple may limit photo and video capture due to privacy concerns. Current reports suggest the product will be unveiled at WWDC 2027 before shipping later that year.

articles.title: AI-GENERATED IMAGES CAN PERFORM AS WELL AS STOCK PHOTOGRAPHY
articles.summary: In a study of 77 participants rating a fictional consulting firm's webpage, AI-generated hero images produced no perception penalty against real stock photos. Ratings for trustworthiness, professionalism, and authenticity were slightly higher for the AI images, though only the authenticity difference reached statistical significance, by 0.4 points. Participants who suspected AI involvement rated pages less favorably, and perceived diversity and representation shaped impressions more than image source.

articles.title: RETHINKING DATA VISUALIZATION: A UX APPROACH TO DASHBOARDS THAT ACTUALLY DRIVES DECISIONS
articles.summary: Roughly 80% of what determines whether a dashboard succeeds happens before any chart is drawn, in defining context, audience and the intended insight. Dashboards fail not because the data is thin but because nobody designed them to answer a specific operational question. A B2B talent-management project shows how radar charts, product-coded color, and a comparison view turned passive reporting into weekly planning.

articles.title: AI CAN'T REPLACE REAL RESEARCH IN EMPATHY MAPPING
articles.summary: Empathy maps are most valuable when they are built from real user research, such as interviews, usability testing, support tickets, and field observations. While AI can generate believable user quotes, emotions, and behaviors, these outputs are assumptions rather than evidence and often lack the specific context that reveals genuine user needs and pain points. AI is best used to organize, cluster, summarize, and synthesize existing research data, not to invent users or fill gaps where research is missing. Relying on AI-generated empathy-map content can create a false sense of understanding and lead teams to make decisions based on fictional users instead of real-world insights.

articles.title: WHAT CRITICAL THINKING MEANS FOR SENIOR DESIGNERS (AND HOW TO APPLY IT)
articles.summary: As AI tools put design output within everyone's reach, the senior designer's job shifts from producing the artifact to justifying it in language non-designers can act on. Spotting that a Figma Make mockup breaks is craft - critical thinking is translating that feeling into behavioral and business consequences. Ask what path a screen requires of the user, then what competes with it.

articles.title: ON UNFURLING INTERFACES
articles.summary: Small interface surfaces work better when they unfold from the edge or control that caused them, rather than arriving through a generic fade and scale. The closed state is a narrow seam built with an inset clip path that preserves the surface's own radius, so corners never square off mid-reveal. Components share a small motion language while keeping their own placement, accessibility, and native lifecycle.

articles.title: GOOGLE'S GEMINI HAS A BRANDING PROBLEM, AND SO DOES THE REST OF AI
articles.summary: Google has given nearly every Gemini feature its own brand, cluttering the app and undercutting its own ease-of-use promise.

articles.title: YAYOI KUSAMA: THE JAPANESE AVANT-GARDE ARTIST WHO CREATED A NEW GENRE OF IMMERSIVE ART
articles.summary: Japanese avant-garde artist Yayoi Kusama's polka dots, nets, and Infinity Mirror Rooms created a genre of immersive art and inspired the minimalist and Pop Art movements.

articles.title: GABRIEL DIOGO ON FOOTBALL, MEMORY, AND THE WARM COLORS OF BRAZIL'S BACKYARDS
articles.summary: Brazilian illustrator Gabriel Diogo left an unfulfilling design career to pursue illustration full-time, building a distinctive style inspired by Brazilian football culture, everyday life, and community identity, ultimately leading to work with brands like Nike while staying rooted in his personal story and creative values.
